sections.heading: Volume and surface area of solids

questions.q: Find the volume of a rectangular prism with dimensions 4 by 5 by 6.
Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 3 and height 10, in terms of $\pi$.
Triangle $ABC$ is similar to triangle $DEF$, with $AB=6$, $DE=9$, and $BC=8$. Find $EF$.
questions.answer: The scale factor is $\dfrac{DE}{AB}=\dfrac{9}{6}=1.5$. So $EF=1.5\times BC=1.5\times8=12$.

questions.q: A tree casts a shadow 20 feet long, while a 6-foot person standing nearby casts a shadow 4 feet long. Find the height of the tree using similar triangles.
questions.answer: Set up a proportion: $\dfrac{\text{tree height}}{20}=\dfrac{6}{4}$. So tree height $=\dfrac{6}{4}\times20=30$ feet.

questions.q: In a right triangle, the angle $\theta$ has an opposite side of length 5 and hypotenuse 13. Find $\sin\theta$, $\cos\theta$, and $\tan\theta$.
A 20-foot ladder leans against a wall, making a $60^\circ$ angle with the ground. Find the height the ladder reaches on the wall, to the nearest tenth.
Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. If one angle measures $65^\circ$, find the measure of its corresponding angle and its co-interior (same-side interior) angle.
questions.answer: The corresponding angle is equal: $65^\circ$. The co-interior angle is supplementary to it (they sum to $180^\circ$): $180^\circ-65^\circ=115^\circ$.

questions.q: A central angle in a circle measures $80^\circ$. Find the measure of the inscribed angle that subtends the same arc.
questions.answer: An inscribed angle is always half the central angle subtending the same arc: $\dfrac{80^\circ}{2}=40^\circ$.

sections.heading: Applying geometry and trigonometry to real-world contexts

questions.q: A surveyor stands 100 feet from the base of a building and measures the angle of elevation to the top as $35^\circ$. Find the height of the building, to the nearest foot.
A square with side length 10 has a circle of radius 4 cut out of its center. Find the remaining area, in terms of $\pi$.
questions.answer: Square area: $10^2=100$. Circle area: $\pi(4)^2=16\pi$. Remaining area: $100-16\pi$.
